newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen up as firms report August data.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen up as firms report August data.

text.p: The Polish bourse is seen rising next week as firms' August earnings results and the month's inflation figure, both seen good, keep the mood positive.
Company earnings, the bulk of them due on Wednesday, are expected to repeat July's performance in proving slightly better than during this year's disappointing first half.
Analysts said Poland's industrial climate, which rose in August for the second straight month, augured both better earnings and a good August industrial production number, the latter due on Tuesday.
Industrial production grew by 4.8 percent in July after falling in June.

"The better industrial climate will likely be taken seriously by institutional investors," said Wojciech Bialek, an analyst at Magnus brokerage, who said the Polish bourse's rise was also linked with recent gains on Western bourses.
The main market's WIG index rose this week to a 30-month high on Friday at 14,296.3 points, up 5.4 percent from last week's close.

Analysts said Monday's August inflation figure, seen around 0.5 percent, could provide grounds for an interest-rate cut as early as late September if inflation that month proved lower than last year's high September number at about three percent.

They said another good sign for stocks was that mass privatisation NFI units hit a correction late this week after rising 44 percent since late August. They said lower NFI turnovers could suggest investors were switching to shares.
Analysts said the main market's biggest loser Stalexport fell 8.5 percent on the week and 9.9 percent on Friday after a court denied its 75-million-zloty claim on interest on overpaid taxes.
But they said its fall should slow next week.
Textile firms led the market this week, finally proving cheap after falling most of the year while the rest of the bourse was enjoying a bull run.
Prochnik, Vistula and Wolczanka rose 22.9 percent, 16.0 percent and 14.4 percent respectively.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of Bank Slaski's 9.8-percent surge on Friday, putting it up 16.7 percent on the week.
